{{Short description|Concept of game theory}}
'''Swap regret''' is a concept from online learning and [[game theory]].  It is a generalization of [[Regret (decision theory)|regret]] in a repeated, ''n''-decision game.

==Definition==
In each round <math>t</math>, the learner chooses decision <math>i</math> with probability <math>x^t_i</math> and the utility for decision <math>i</math> is <math>p^t_i</math>. A learner's ''swap-regret'' is defined to be the following:

: <math>\mbox{swap-regret}=
\sum_{i=1}^n \max_{j \leq n}\sum_{t=1}^T x^t_i \cdot (p^t_j-p^t_i).</math>

Intuitively, it is how much a player could improve by switching each occurrence of decision ''i'' to the best decision ''j'' possible in [[hindsight]]. The swap regret is always nonnegative. Swap regret is useful for computing [[correlated equilibrium|correlated equilibria]].
